name: Michael Madhusudan Dutt
credit: Michael Madhusudan Dutt, 19th-century photograph · Public domain (Wikimedia Commons)
bio: Michael Madhusudan Dutt (1824–1873) was a Bengali poet and dramatist born at Sagardari in Jessore. He studied at Hindu College, Calcutta, took the name Michael on converting to Christianity in 1843, and spent years in Madras writing in English before returning to Bengali in the late 1850s on the urging of friends.

He introduced blank verse (amitrakshar chhanda) and the sonnet into Bengali. His Tilottamasambhab Kavya (1860), Meghnadbadh Kavya (1861), Brajangana (1861) and Birangana Kavya (1862) transformed the language of Bengali poetry, and the nine-sarga Meghnadbadh Kavya, which retells the Ramayana story from the side of Ravana's son Meghnad, is his masterpiece.
